## What shipped

`src/router/index.ts` — the Router module. Exports `EmailCategory`, `RouterErrorCode`, `RouterError`, `isRouterError`, and `createRouter()`. The factory reads all three category env vars at construction (eager snapshot), validates them against the provider registry, instantiates each provider once, and freezes the map. `resolve(category)` is a pure frozen-map lookup. 27 tests covering all 6 WU acceptance criteria plus memoisation and `isRouterError` guard paths.

## What didn't ship

Nothing deferred. All acceptance criteria met in the first pass.

## Notes / observations

The architect's design-it-twice produced a clear winner — Design B (eager snapshot) was obviously correct given the existing `validateEnv()` pattern in `src/lib/env.ts` and the Vercel serverless lifecycle. Design A (lazy) was worth naming only to confirm there was a real choice; the tester's note that "SES client must be mocked before import" reinforces why eager instantiation at module load time is the right shape for a frozen provider map.

The `UNKNOWN_CATEGORY` NIT is worth remembering: defensive guards in a typed language will often be unreachable in practice. The architect's brief explicitly called for it as a safety net for untyped callers; the reviewer correctly flagged it as a NIT rather than a blocker. This is the right call — the guard adds one line and two test cases for a category of runtime errors that TypeScript can't prevent in mixed-language callers.
